description: One undo step: `command` as it was applied, its `inverse`, and the `origin` it came from.
title: HistoryEntry

ActuateEntry.description:
Command `command` on `actuator` during `[start, end)` seconds of simulated time.

`command` is the fraction of the actuator's full command, in [-1, 1] for a motor (sign is direction) and
[0, 1] for a thruster. What full command means physically comes from the part (B-03b, B-03c, X-01b, X-01c).
One badge and source cover the entry. `id` names the entry inside the schedule (unique there): commands
that edit an entry name it by id, never by position, so a reordered or partly accepted batch cannot change
a different entry than the one meant.
ActuateEntry.title: ActuateEntry

Actuator.description:
Something on `instance` that a command drives. A motor drives one joint (`joint`); a thruster has none.

`supply` (B-03d) is the instance the actuator draws from: a motor from a `battery` part, a thruster from a `tank`
part (`PartRole`). `None` means the actuator is not metered (nothing runs out). Several actuators may share one
supply; what it holds is spent by all of them (`kinetra_engine.parts.supply`).
Actuator.title: Actuator

AddAssumption.description:
Add an assumption. It must be `editable`: one that is not could never be changed or removed again, so its
inverse would not apply.
AddAssumption.title: AddAssumption

AddControlEntry.description: Add a schedule entry. `index` is only where it goes in the list; the entry is known by its `id`.
AddControlEntry.title: AddControlEntry

AddPartDef.description: Put a part definition into the project (`DesignSpec` carries the definitions it uses).
AddPartDef.title: AddPartDef

Assumption.description: One assumption of the verdict, as the human-review panel shows it.

key.description: Stable machine key, e.g. 'vehicle_mass'. Verdict sensitivities cite it.
key.title: Key

Assumption.title: Assumption

AxisExpr.description:
A length in metres: `offset + sum(factor * param)`. A snap point coordinate in the part's local frame, or a
dimension of a shape component (`shape.py`). Every `param` is a length parameter of the part.
AxisExpr.title: AxisExpr

Box.description: Rectangular block. `size_*` are full extents [m] along the component's local x, y, z.
Box.title: Box

BreakThreshold.description: Joint load [N] above which the joint releases. A simplified model, not FEM (plan 4.6).
BreakThreshold.title: BreakThreshold

ClearParameter.description: Unset a parameter of an instance: it takes the part's default again.
ClearParameter.title: ClearParameter

CommandBatch.description:
Edits applied in order as one: all of them or none (`client-adapter.md` C2). Every intermediate state
must be a valid `Project` (see the module docstring).
CommandBatch.title: CommandBatch

Curve.description: Piecewise-linear `y(x)`: at least two points, `x` strictly increasing, in `x_unit` and `y_unit`.
Curve.title: Curve

Cylinder.description: Solid circular cylinder. `radius` and `length` [m]; the axis is the component's local z.
Cylinder.title: Cylinder

FixedDistribution.description: No spread: Monte-Carlo uses the nominal.
FixedDistribution.title: FixedDistribution

Instance.description:
One placed part. Parameters not listed take the `PartDef` default. `material` is optional: a part whose
mass is declared by its own specs needs none; `None` means no material is assigned.
Instance.title: Instance

Joint.description:
A connection between two snap points of two different instances. `a` is the parent side by convention.

`axis` (hinge and slider): the line the one free motion is about or along, in the frame of the `a` snap point
(`JointAxis`). `None` is +Z of that frame (`DEFAULT_JOINT_AXIS`). A fixed joint has no motion and so no axis.
`limits` are optional (`None`: unlimited, as a wheel axle) and not allowed on a fixed joint; they bound the joint
coordinate, which is 0 at the saved pose (`JointLimits`).
`break_threshold` is optional (`None`: never breaks).
Joint.title: Joint

JointAxis.description:
The direction a hinge turns about or a slider moves along: a unit vector in the frame of the snap point of
the joint's `a` end (the parent side), the same frame a snap point's `orientation` gives. One badge and source
cover the vector. The sense is right-handed for a hinge (positive angle turns `b` counter-clockwise seen from
the tip of the axis) and positive travel is along the vector for a slider. `-axis` describes the same line of
motion with the sign of the coordinate (and so of its limits and of a motor command) flipped.
JointAxis.title: JointAxis

JointLimits.description:
Travel limits of the joint coordinate: rad for a hinge, m for a slider. `lower < upper`.

The coordinate is 0 at the saved pose, so the saved pose must be inside its own limits: `lower <= 0 <= upper`
(a joint saved outside its travel would start in violation of its own limit). Both ends are inclusive.
JointLimits.title: JointLimits

MoveInstance.description: Set the stored world pose of one instance.
MoveInstance.title: MoveInstance

NamedCurve.description: A curve a part defines under a name (`torque_speed` for a motor, `thrust` for a thruster).
NamedCurve.title: NamedCurve

Origin.description:
Which input path sent a command (`client-adapter.md` 3.5): the person's mouse or keyboard, the agent's
accepted proposal, a confirmed voice sentence, an XR hand or controller, the MCP server.
Origin.title: Origin

ParamDef.description: A named parameter of the part with its default and allowed range, all in `unit`.
ParamDef.title: ParamDef

ParamTerm.description: `factor * <value of parameter param>`. The parameter must be a length.
ParamTerm.title: ParamTerm

ParamValue.description: The value of one of the part's parameters for this instance. Unit and range are the `ParamDef`'s.
ParamValue.title: ParamValue

PartRole.description:
What a part is for, where the simulation needs to know (B-03b). A part without a role is only a body.

The actuator on an instance must fit its part's role (`designspec.py`): a motor actuator drives a `motor` part, a
thruster actuator a `thruster` part. What a role requires of the definition is checked by `PartDef` (the
required curves and specs), so a part that says `motor` always has the numbers a motor needs.
PartRole.title: PartRole

Pose.description: World pose of an instance's part frame. One badge and source cover the whole pose.
Pose.title: Pose

Quantity.description: One physical number with its unit, badge and source.
Quantity.title: Quantity

RemoveActuator.description: Remove an actuator with its schedule entries.
RemoveActuator.title: RemoveActuator

RemoveAssumption.description: Remove the assumption with this key. Refused (`not_editable`) when it is not `editable`.
RemoveAssumption.title: RemoveAssumption

RemoveControlEntry.description: Remove the schedule entry with this id.
RemoveControlEntry.title: RemoveControlEntry

RemoveInstance.description:
Delete an instance with its joints, the actuators on it, on those joints or drawing from it (a battery or tank),
and their schedule entries.
RemoveInstance.title: RemoveInstance

RemoveJoint.description: Release a joint, with the actuators that drive it and their schedule entries.
RemoveJoint.title: RemoveJoint

RemoveMaterialDef.description: Take a material definition out. Rejected while an instance or a terrain prop uses it.
RemoveMaterialDef.title: RemoveMaterialDef

RemovePartDef.description: Take a part definition out. Rejected while an instance uses it.
RemovePartDef.title: RemovePartDef

ReplaceControlEntry.description: Replace the schedule entry with the same id (`entry.id`), in place.
ReplaceControlEntry.title: ReplaceControlEntry

ReplaceJoint.description:
Replace the joint with the same id, in place: same position, and the actuators and schedule entries on it
stay. Changes its limits, break threshold, kind or ends. Rejected if the new joint no longer suits what is on
it (a motor on a joint that is fixed now, a motor whose instance is no longer at an end).
ReplaceJoint.title: ReplaceJoint

ReplaceMaterialDef.description: Replace the material definition with the same id, in place (instances and terrain props keep using it).
ReplaceMaterialDef.title: ReplaceMaterialDef

ReplacePartDef.description:
Replace the part definition with the same id, in place. Instances keep using it, so the new definition
must still suit every one of them (their parameters, their joints' snap points): else the command is
rejected with the validator's sentence and the offending ref.
ReplacePartDef.title: ReplacePartDef

SelectPlanet.description: Put the project on another planet, by id. The planet's constants are not part of any command.
SelectPlanet.title: SelectPlanet

SetAssumption.description:
Replace the assumption with the same `key`, in place. Refused (`not_editable`) when the stored one is not
`editable`, and when the new one would change `editable`.
SetAssumption.title: SetAssumption

SetInstanceMaterial.description: Assign a material of the project to an instance; `None` assigns none.
SetInstanceMaterial.title: SetInstanceMaterial

SetParameter.description:
Set a parameter of an instance (unit and range are the part's). `index` is where a parameter that is not
set yet goes in the instance's list; for one that is set already it must be absent.
SetParameter.title: SetParameter

Shape.description:
The recipe: one or more components. At least one is `add`; ids are unique.

The offsets and factors inside the expressions are plain numbers; like a snap point's pose, the recipe carries
one badge and source for all of them (who drew these dimensions: `declared`, or `cite` with a drawing, ...).
Shape.title: Shape

SnapPoint.description:
A place where this part can attach to another. `kind` and `accepts` are compatibility tags (B-04b matches them).

`position` is in metres in the part's local frame and may follow length parameters; `orientation` is the
local frame of the snap point. Badge and source cover the whole pose.
SnapPoint.title: SnapPoint

SnapRef.description: A snap point of a placed instance.
SnapRef.title: SnapRef

Source.description:
Where a value comes from.

`ref` is what was cited, declared or run: a document, a datasheet, a run id, or the reason a default was chosen
(for an estimate: the method and its inputs). `locator` is where inside it (table, page, section). `url` is a
link when there is one. `license` (SPDX expression over the repo allowlist, `spdx.py`) and `declared_by` / `declared_at` feed the badge popover
(`ValueBadges`, 인용 and 사용자 선언); `Provenance` allows each only on its own badge.
Source.title: Source

SpecDef.description: A named specification (사양): no-load speed, rated thrust, capacity ... Name and unit are the part's.
SpecDef.title: SpecDef

Unit.description: Closed unit vocabulary (SI, written the way the JSON carries it).
Unit.title: Unit

WorldPosition.description: A position in metres, world frame.
WorldPosition.title: WorldPosition
